subject: Cross-border ownership mapping & KMS custody evidence request
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: AtlasCloud Security <security@atlascloud.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Cross-border ownership mapping & KMS custody evidence request

Hi team —

Following our call this morning with ClientCo procurement, they’ve flagged two items in the draft transfer annex that need concrete evidence before their legal ops will sign the DPA:

1) Ownership boundary for PII processed by Redwood in multi-region deployments (they want a single-page matrix showing which tenants/data types stay in EU, which traverse to US/third countries, and which are pseudonymized before export).
2) KMS custody and split-key controls for dedicated/private deployments (they asked for an attestation or diagram that shows where customer keys are generated, stored, and used in the inference path).

I attached the current transfer annex draft and a first-pass KMS diagram (kms-custody-diagram-v2.png). Can AtlasCloud provide their standard KMS attestation PDF and confirm whether their managed key flow involves any subprocessor handoff? ClientCo is particularly sensitive to any key escrow or third-party backup of keys.

Ask: Aditya / Grace — can you add a short paragraph to the annex that: a) enumerates the PII categories (identifiers, health metadata, support traces) and b) states whether we pseudonymize/strip or allow tokenized transit for each? Laura — legal: if we change wording from "we may transfer" to "we will restrict transfers to...unless customer consents", does that materially alter our risk profile for other prospects?

Next steps: if AtlasCloud can drop their attestation by EOD Wednesday (8/15), I’ll route to ClientCo legal along with the annex.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Security & Privacy Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20280813-transfer-annex-draft.pdf (application/pdf), kms-custody-diagram-v2.png (image/png)

From: AtlasCloud Security <security@atlascloud.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Aug 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cross-border ownership mapping & KMS custody evidence request

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks for the clear summary. We attached our standard KMS attestation (atlas-kms-attestation-2028-07.pdf). Key facts in brief:
- Keys are customer-generated in our HSM tenancy; AtlasCloud never retains plaintext copies.
- Backups are encrypted with a customer-only root key when customers opt into managed backup; otherwise backups are disabled.
- We do not hand keys to subprocessors; certain telemetry and usage logs are stored in a separate logging cluster (see attestation section 3.2) — those logs contain only key IDs, not materialized keys.

Regarding cross-border movement: our standard practice is to pin customer keys to the region of generation. Customer data may be routed for inference to a compatible region by policy, but when a customer requires regional residency we provide a dedicated tenancy option that enforces egress controls. We confirm there is no automatic key escrow.

We can provide a short CSV mapping of regions -> storage tenancy -> key custody by EOD Wednesday. If you want that routed to ClientCo directly, give us the HubSpot deal id or their procurement contact.

—Arun Patel
Director, Security Engineering | AtlasCloud

Attachment: atlas-kms-attestation-2028-07.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Aug 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cross-border ownership mapping & KMS custody evidence request

Kimberly / Grace —

Thanks Atlas — that attestation is helpful. Quick updates on the annex text: I drafted a concise PII matrix and pushed it to the Drive link you listed ("transfer annex"). The table rows are the PII categories ClientCo cares about: user_identifiers, device_signals, healthcare_annotations, support_traces. For each row I added columns: residency_default, transit_behavior (pseudonymize/tokenize/cleartext), kms_binding (regional/dedicated/none).

Two clarifications I need from legal before I commit:
- "Pseudonymize" vs "tokenize" language: we currently pseudonymize support_traces and tokenized embeddings for analytics. Are those terms precise enough or should we define them in the DPA annex?
- WRT the residency statement: I wrote "Customer-residency enforced for Dedicated Tenancy where required by contract." Laura, if we say "enforced by contract" do we need any additional operational SLAs or will the dedicated tenancy product terms suffice?

I can turn the table into a one-page SVG for ClientCo and send with Atlas' attestation. Grace — can you review the mapping of healthcare_annotations (I know we apply extra retention minimization there).

-Aditya
Senior Privacy Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, AtlasCloud Security <security@atlascloud.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@clientco.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Aug 2028 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cross-border ownership mapping & KMS custody evidence request

Thanks everyone — quick legal position and suggested language.

1) Definitions: please include definitions in the annex for "pseudonymize" and "tokenize" (one sentence each) and add a parenthetical example. That prevents ambiguity and aligns with GDPR expectations.

2) Residency wording: the phrase "enforced by contract" is acceptable, but add an explicit operational appendix reference: "Dedicated Tenancy residency enforcement (Operational Appendix A)". That appendix should enumerate the controls (IP allowlists, egress firewall rules, logging and periodic attestation). If we cannot produce Appendix A at signing, we must offer a targeted SLA milestone (e.g., Appendix delivered within 30 days post-signature) rather than leave it unspecified.

3) KMS attestation: AtlasCloud's attestation is sufficient for ClientCo's initial intake. However, to be thorough we should also include our end-to-end key flow diagram that shows that we never move plaintext keys out of HSM boundary — Kimberly, please embed a short note in the annex referencing kms-custody-diagram-v2.png and Atlas' attestation.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Action items: Kimberly to produce the one-page PII matrix SVG and a cover email to ClientCo; Aditya to add definitions to the annex; Grace to confirm handling of healthcare_annotations retention sentence. AtlasCloud to provide the CSV mapping by EOD Wednesday if possible (HubSpot-Deal-45321).
